author: Nate Miller
title: Danny Young (elbow) activated from IL
desc: Danny Young (elbow) was activated from the IL ahead of Friday's game against the Mets.
impact: Young will join the Braves at the start of a series against his former club. The lefty, who signed with the Braves this past December, worked in 10 games for the Mets last season, putting up a 4.32 ERA and 13-3 K/BB ratio across 8 1/3 innings.

author: Nate Miller
title: Anthony Molina heads back to bigs
desc: Anthony Molina was recalled from Triple-A Gwinnett on Friday.
impact: Molina will rejoin the Braves' bullpen ahead of Friday's series opener against the Mets. The 24-year-old righty has made three appearances for the Braves this season, giving up four runs (three earned) over five innings.

author: Nate Miller
title: Dominic Smith drives in three runs Thursday evening
desc: Dominic Smith went 1-for-4 with a three-run double in Thursday's 11-5 loss to the Cardinals.
impact: With the Braves facing an early three-run deficit, their offense briefly came to life in the first inning Thursday, scoring five while bringing 10 batters to the plate. Smith delivered the big knock of the inning, as he stepped up with the bases loaded and rifled a liner off the foot of St. Louis pitcher Dustin May. The ball would ricochet all the way into right field and clear the bases. Smith is now up to 35 RBI on the year, and perhaps he can snap out of a long cold streak.

author: Nate Miller
title: Hurston Waldrep recovers after shaky first inning
desc: Hurston Waldrep allowed three runs on five hits and one walk while striking out four over 5 1/3 innings in Thursday's 11-5 loss to the Cardinals.
impact: Waldrep made his first start of the season for the Braves on Thursday, and just his second appearance overall after spending the first few months on the IL. The young righty had a rocky first inning, letting the first two Cardinals hitters to reach base before serving up a three-run homer to Jordan Walker later in the frame. However, Waldrep impressively recovered over the next four-plus innings, keeping the Cardinals' bats from adding any additional runs. Expectations remain high for Waldrep after he posted a 2.88 ERA and 1.19 WHIP with 55 strikeouts across 56 1/3 innings as a rookie in 2025.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Jacob Misiorowski provides mixed results on mound in loss to Reds
desc: Jacob Misiorowski allowed five runs (one earned) on five hits while striking out 10 over five innings in Thursday's loss to the Reds.
impact: Misiorowski continues a strong stretch on the mound of late, striking out seven or more in each of his last 13 trips to the mound. The right-hander continues to reward fantasy managers with an elite starting option at the top of the Brewers rotation, carrying a 1.47 ERA and 0.78 WHIP with a 9-4 record and 13.5 K/9 ratio across 17 starts.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Christian Yelich swipes base in loss to Reds
desc: Christian Yelich went 0-for-3 in Thursday's 7-2 loss to the Reds with one walk and one stolen base.
impact: Yelich has heated up of late, getting on base in each of his last four contests. The 34-year-old has fought consistency issues for much of the season in the Brewers lineup, hitting .252 with five home runs, 26 RBI, 38 runs scored, and six stolen bases across 52 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: David Hamilton steals base in loss to Reds
desc: David Hamilton went 1-for-2 in a loss to the Reds with one stolen base.
impact: Hamilton has provided mixed results at the plate, picking up hits in three of his last six contests. The infielder remains one of the more inconsistent options when in the Brewers lineup for manager Pat Murphy, batting .235 with three home runs, 13 RBI, 31 runs scored, and 18 stolen bases across 71 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Garrett Mitchell homers in loss to Reds
desc: Garrett Mitchell went 1-for-3 in loss to the Reds with a solo home run and one walk.
impact: Mitchell continues a productive stretch at the plate, driving in runs in five of his last seven contests. The outfielder offers manager Pat Murphy another stable bat in the Brewers lineup to this point, batting .265 with seven homers, 40 RBI, 36 runs scored, and six steals through 75 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Jake McCarthy drives in four as Rockies outslug Marlins
desc: Jake McCarthy went 2-for-4 in Thursday's 14-4 win over the Marlins with a home run, three runs scored, four RBI, and one walk.
impact: McCarthy continues a torrid stretch at the plate, recording hits in 13 of his last 16 contests. The outfielder provides manager Warren Schaeffer with one of the more stable options in the Rockies lineup, posting an .829 OPS with seven home runs, 41 RBI, 34 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases across 73 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Mickey Moniak racks up three hits in win over Marlins
desc: Mickey Moniak went 3-for-5 in Thursday's 14-4 win over the Marlins with a home run, a double, three runs scored, and two RBI.
impact: Moniak has flashed his power stroke of late, homering in each of his last three contests. The outfielder offers manager Warren Schaeffer one of the more dynamic bats in the Rockies lineup, carrying a .951 OPS with 15 homers, 37 RBI, 28 runs scored, and one steal through 53 games.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Michael Lorenzen fights control in abrreviated outing
desc: Michael Lorenzen allowed four earned runs on four hits and six walks while striking out one over 4 1/3 innings in Thursday's win over the Marlins.
impact: Lorenzen has struggled to miss opposing bats of late, allowing three earned runs or more in six of his last nine contests. The right-hander remains one of many underwhelming starting options in the Rockies rotation for manager Warren Schaeffer, posting a 6.91 ERA and 1.81 WHIP with a 3-9 record and 2.1 K/BB ratio across 19 appearances.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Nathan Eovaldi strikes out nine in fourth straight win
desc: Nathan Eovaldi earned the win Thursday against the Tigers after allowing three runs on six hits and one walk over five innings. He struck out nine and generated 18 swinging strikes. Eovaldi opened with four scoreless frames before surrendering two home runs in the fifth.
impact: Eovaldi has won four consecutive starts and matched his season high with nine strikeouts for the third straight outing. He is tentatively scheduled to face the Angels at home next.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Josh Smith homers off bench Thursday
desc: Josh Smith went 2-for-2 with a home run and two RBI in Thursday's 10-4 win over the Tigers. He entered as a pinch hitter for Justin Foscue in the sixth inning and immediately delivered a solo homer to right field before adding an RBI infield single in the seventh.
impact: Smith was recalled Wednesday after spending time in the minors late in June and has gone 3-for-4 across two games since returning. He had struggled for much of the season before the demotion.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Elias Diaz homers in second straight game
desc: Elias Diaz went 2-for-4 with a solo home run, a double, a walk, and two runs scored in Thursday's 10-4 win over the Tigers. He opened the scoring with a 414-foot solo shot in the second inning, giving him homers in consecutive games after going 18 contests without one following his June 5 arrival in Texas.
impact: Diaz served as the designated hitter Thursday and has started five of the Rangers' last six games, including four starts behind the plate. His recent playing time suggests he is gaining a more regular place in the lineup.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Evan Carter homers off bench in win
desc: Evan Carter went 2-for-2 with a solo home run and two runs scored in Thursday's 10-4 win over the Tigers. He entered as a pinch hitter in the seventh inning, singled and scored, then added a solo homer in the eighth.
impact: Carter is 4-for-11 with one home run and three additional runs scored across four games since returning from the injured list. He began Thursday on the bench against a left-handed starter.
